description:
The empty-input boundary of CBTRN01C, and the most extreme form of its post-end-of-file lookup: DALYTRAN is seeded as a dataset that EXISTS and holds NO row, so the very first READ meets end of file and there is no record for the unguarded lookup that follows to be stale FROM. This is the shortest fingerprint in the folder - four DISPLAY lines, twelve file verbs, one sequential read, one keyed read, and nothing written anywhere. MAIN-PARA at app/cbl/CBTRN01C.cbl:155-197 in order: :156 displays the start banner; :157-162 open the six files and every one of the six succeeds silently, an OPEN INPUT of an existing-but-empty sequential file reporting '00' rather than an error, which is precisely why the dataset is declared empty here and not left unbound - an unbound dataset is the OPEN-FAILURE scenario and belongs to case19, not to this case; the loop at :164 is entered because END-OF-DAILY-TRANS-FILE still holds its declared 'N' from :146, the guard at :165 passes, and 1000-DALYTRAN-GET-NEXT at :203-225 issues the read. The status ladder at :204-212 takes its MIDDLE arm in source order - not '00', then '10' - so :208 moves 16 into APPL-RESULT, the 88 APPL-EOF condition at :144 matches at :216, and :217 moves 'Y' into END-OF-DAILY-TRANS-FILE. NO ABEND: end of file is a normal terminator on this path and the :219-222 arm, which is the one that displays 'ERROR READING DAILY TRANSACTION FILE' and reaches Z-ABEND-PROGRAM, is not taken (gates G30 and G47). The inner guard at :167 is now false, so the record echo at :168 does NOT happen - and the three statements at :170-172 run anyway, because that guard closed at :169 and covers only the DISPLAY. 2000-LOOKUP-XREF at :227-239 therefore probes the cross reference with whatever DALYTRAN-CARD-NUM holds, takes INVALID KEY - FileStatus '23' - displays 'INVALID CARD NUMBER FOR XREF' at :232 and moves 4 into WS-XREF-READ-STATUS at :233. The test at :173 consequently fails, the ELSE at :180-184 runs, and the account read is NEVER ISSUED: no 'SUCCESSFUL READ OF ACCOUNT FILE' and no 'INVALID ACCOUNT NUMBER FOUND' can appear, which is why ACCTFILE is seeded with a real row it never reaches. The loop then exits on the 'Y' flag, :188-193 close the six files silently, and :195 displays the end banner. THE ONE GENUINE AMBIGUITY, RESOLVED AND DOCUMENTED RATHER THAN ABSORBED (practice B12): DALYTRAN-RECORD was never populated, because COPY CVTRA06Y at :99 places it in WORKING-STORAGE with no VALUE clause, and IBM COBOL leaves an un-VALUEd WORKING-STORAGE item formally undefined - so there is no single 'captured' truth to reproduce and a case that asserted one would be asserting an undefined value. The convention adopted here is that such an area is SPACE-INITIALISED, which makes DALYTRAN-CARD-NUM (CVTRA06Y bytes 263-278) sixteen spaces and DALYTRAN-ID (bytes 1-16) sixteen spaces. The choice is not arbitrary: it is the one the Java layer actually guarantees, since common.FixedWidthRecord allocates a span at its declared record length and fills it with the space byte, and TransactionPostingJob holds its DALYTRAN-RECORD as exactly such a declared-value area before any read. Choosing spaces makes this case reproducible on every run (practice B7) instead of pinning whatever an undefined area happened to contain. LINE THREE IS WHERE A HAND COUNT GOES WRONG. :181-183 is ONE DISPLAY of three literals and two operands, concatenated with no separator beyond what the literals themselves carry: 'CARD NUMBER ' ends in a space, ' COULD NOT BE VERIFIED. SKIPPING TRANSACTION ID-' begins with a space and ends in a hyphen with no trailing space, and the two PIC X(16) operands contribute sixteen blanks each. Measured from the source rather than counted by eye, those literals are 12 and 48 characters, so the line is 12 + 16 + 48 + 16 = 92 characters and its two sixteen-blank runs - one interior, one trailing - are significant and must never be trimmed (practice B8). The cross reference is seeded with cardxref.txt row 21 (zero-based 20), card 4859452612877065, specifically so that the miss is a genuine key miss against a NON-EMPTY dataset rather than a vacuous one: not one of the fifty fixture rows begins with sixteen spaces - every one opens with a sixteen-digit card number - so the blank probe cannot accidentally match. That row is seeded at the 36 bytes the fixture actually holds and is NOT pre-padded; the declared CARDXREF_FILLER_PAD_36_TO_50 normalisation supplies CVACT03Y's absent FILLER X(14) once, at seed time, and the final state then pins all four spans by name - 16 + 9 + 11 + 14 = the whole 50 bytes, so no byte goes unasserted (gate G16, risk R-F). acctdata.txt row 7 (zero-based 6) is pinned as a full 300-byte image, whose FILLER X(178) occupies bytes 123-300 and whose ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE keeps the copybook's own misspelling (requirement I1); the width is what proves every FILLER span was emitted (gates G19 and G21). DALYTRAN, CUSTFILE, CARDFILE and TRANFILE are each declared empty rather than omitted, which is a different assertion: an omitted dataset is one the case says nothing about, while an empty one positively states that a real dataset was opened and held no row - the only way to reach a FILE STATUS of '10' on a first READ, and what makes 'opened and never read' a statement about datasets that exist. CUSTFILE and CARDFILE are never read by any statement in the program and TRANFILE is never read and never written; :158-160 open them and :189-191 close them, and that is all. expectedWrites is EMPTY as a positive assertion rather than an absence of interest - the source contains zero WRITE and zero REWRITE statements and opens all six files OPEN INPUT - and the six writes-channel expectations below say the same thing per dataset at its exact copybook width. THE PROGRAM THE PROMPT NAMES TransactionPostingJob POSTS NOTHING (rule R1, practice B4). RETURN-CODE is 0: CBTRN01C contains no MOVE statement targeting RETURN-CODE anywhere, APPL-RESULT becomes 16 only to satisfy 88 APPL-EOF, and the CALL 'CEE3ABD' at :473 is unreached. jobParameters is empty because CBTRN01C is this migration's orphan - no EXEC PGM=CBTRN01C exists in app/jcl or app/proc, so there is no PARM for one to come from and the job carries no trigger (gate G13, requirement I4). BASELINE PROVENANCE, practice B12: these expected values are STATICALLY DERIVED from app/cbl/CBTRN01C.cbl read paragraph by paragraph - :164-186, :202-225 and :227-239 - and cross-checked against the copybook byte layouts in app/cpy (CVTRA06Y 350, CVACT03Y 50, CVACT01Y 300, every offset mechanically diffable by eye - practice B11) and against the real ASCII fixtures. They were NEVER captured from, recorded against or replayed from any execution of the legacy COBOL, because executing it is empirically impossible in this environment: no z/OS or CICS runtime, an indexed-file handler the available compiler reports as disabled, and no Language Environment CEE* services. AAP section 0.7.6 records eight independently verified blockers; the substitution changes the PROVENANCE of the expected values and nothing else, and is escalated for explicit user confirmation as risk R-A rather than quietly absorbed. A NUMBERING DIVERGENCE, likewise recorded rather than silently corrected (practice B4): CBTRN01CParityTest currently builds its twenty scenarios in code and does not load this directory - its cases() method is the seam through which these fixtures would be adopted - and in that in-code set the same degenerate empty-input form is numbered case04 while case05 is a full pass over all 300 fixture rows. This declarative fixture set numbers the empty-input boundary case05 and the open-failure scenario case19. The two plans agree on behaviour and differ only in which ordinal carries which scenario, so anyone adopting the seam should reconcile the ordinals deliberately rather than discover the difference as a diff. Bytes are US-ASCII, stated and never taken from the platform default, and nothing here reads a clock, draws an unpredictable value or consults the environment - CBTRN01C reads no clock, so the fingerprint is identical on every run (practices B7 and B8). review_rules returns exactly one line, "No user rules provided.", so no user rule governs this fixture; the binding standard is the enterprise-practice set, and its absence is not licence to assert less. Gates carried: G13, G15, G16, G18, G19, G21, G30 (the :204-212 ladder taking its '10' arm), G47 (the '10' sequential read outcome and the '23' keyed-read outcome) and G51 (the tasklet body is driven directly, with no JobLauncher and no HTTP layer in the path). G32 does not apply: CBTRN01C contains zero GO TO statements.

THE READ SEQUENCE, DECLARED RATHER THAN INFERRED. expectedOperations names every read this run must issue, in order and with the key it is given, and it says three things no byte fingerprint can. First, WHICH VERB: the daily file's read is readNext because :203 reads sequentially and takes whatever record is next, while the cross reference and the account are read at :229 and :243 by a key the program built - a translation that turned either keyed read into a browse would produce identical SYSOUT. Second, HOW MANY: there is always one readNext more than there are records, because the loop at :164-186 reads again to learn it is at end of file, and the lookup that follows sits at :170-172 OUTSIDE the guard that closed at :169 - so the last lookup runs on the card number the previous record left in WORKING-STORAGE. Third, WITH WHAT: the key is recorded as declared, so on the trailing lookup it is the PREVIOUS record's card number, and on a run whose daily file was empty it is absent entirely because the record area never held anything. Every entry here was derived from this case's own expected DISPLAY lines - one echo per record at :168, one lookup block per iteration - and never from a run.
